Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.

# LDO-QUIET-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.2 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 1e-08 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

PSRR, bidirectional line excursion/recovery and output noise are scored in every
public and independent group. Each nominal group contains 11 native processes:
three DC, three load profiles, two PSRR, two noise and one line profile.
There are 198 public plus 33 independent cases, with no duplicate nominal
characterization stage. Standalone noise_low/noise_high/line/PSRR cost one each.
Line uses the tighter line excursion limit; its initial and recovery bands are
the fixed DC/recovery bands. Repeated endpoint trajectories across starting-VIN
labels are repetitions, not extra coverage.

Output noise integrates native output voltage ASD squared from 10 Hz to 100 kHz
at 50 points/decade. Use a linear-frequency trapezoidal PSD integral and then its
square root. VREF and load are ideal noiseless sources. Keep the spectrum in
V/sqrt(Hz), integrated output in V RMS, and a valid regulated OP. Negative ASD,
missing band endpoints, sparse/nonfinite data and nonregulating OP cannot pass.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

# Netlist grammar

Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.

Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

Bash
1: # Netlist grammar
2: 
3: Use local .subckt/.ends, local .param and constant arithmetic + - * / in braces.
4: Elements are X for approved MOS wrappers or local subcircuits, R and C. No includes, models, sources or analyses.
5: MOS order is drain gate source body. NFET body connects to VSS; PFET body connects to VIN.
6: Use VSS instead of global node 0. Names are case-insensitive. Full-line * comments and + continuation are supported.
7: SKY130 W/L are bare numeric micrometres; nf=1 and integer m=1..32.
8: ADM45 W/L use SI or SPICE suffixes; integer mult=1..32, implicit nf=1, default ad/as/pd/ps=0.
9: R/C use SI or suffixes (M is milli, meg is mega). Positive R=1..1e8 ohm, C>=1e-15 F; total C and MOS W*L must satisfy spec.json.
10: Maximum source 65536 bytes, 2048 statements, 32 local subcircuits, depth 12, 2048 expansion visits, 512 expanded elements.
11: Only used subcircuits are allowed. Validation checks each physical copy and each technology's geometry domain.
12: 
13: Per-polarity domains (micrometres), intersect all tt/ss/ff sections and W<=100, L>=0.15:

import re,json
s=open('devices.md').read()
m=re.search(r'"'```json'"\\s*(\\{.*?\\})\\s*"'```'"',s,re.S)
print('has domains',bool(m))
d=json.loads(m.group(1))
for pol,procdata in d.items():
 print(pol)
 for proc, rects in procdata.items():
  lo_l=max(x['lmin'] for x in rects); hi_l=min(x['lmax'] for x in rects)
  print(proc, 'rects',len(rects),'Lglobal',lo_l,hi_l, 'Wglobal',max(x['wmin'] for x in rects),min(x['wmax'] for x in rects))
 print('candidate W/L accepted')
 for w,l in [(10,1),(100,.5),(100,1),(20,2),(40,.5),(8,.5),(7,.5),(50,1),(25,1)]:
  ok=all(any(x['wmin']<=w<=x['wmax'] and x['lmin']<=l<=x['lmax'] for x in rects) for rects in procdata.values())
  print(w,l,ok)

MODEL

The spec’s main pinch points are the 1.4 V minimum input, the 2 mA load, fast recovery, low light-load overhead, and supply rejection. I’m starting with a PMOS pass device, a high-side differential error stage, a light resistor divider, and a compensated gate driver; I’ll validate the syntax and use the bundled nominal run to guide revisions.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > dut.spice <<'EOF'
.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS reference current and differential pair
RBIAS PB VSS 50k
XPBIAS PB PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPTAIL CS PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Feedback divider targets VOUT=2*VREF
RFTOP VOUT FB 100k
RFBOT FB VSS 100k
* P-channel input pair; N-channel mirror produces an increasing output
* command when VOUT is below target.
XPMREF N1 VREF CS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=40 l=2
XPMFB N2 FB CS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=40 l=2
XNMREF N1 N1 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=2
XNMFDB N2 N1 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=2
* NMOS driver sinks the pass gate; resistor pulls it safely off.
XDRV PGATE N2 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=1
RGP VIN PGATE 100k
* High-side pass device
XPASS VOUT PGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=16
* Miller compensation with a series damping resistor
RCOMP N2 NC 10k
CCOMP NC PGATE 30p
.ends DUT
EOF
atb-client validate"

/usr/local/bin/atb-client: Python script, ASCII text executable
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Participant measurement and submission client; authority stays with the broker."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import socket
import sys


def parser():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='atb-client',description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument('--request',type=Path,help='Read a complete request from a JSON file')
    sub=p.add_subparsers(dest='command')
    for name in ('help','status','validate'):
        sub.add_parser(name)
    for name in ('estimate','measure'):
        s=sub.add_parser(name)
        if name=='measure':s.add_argument('--id',dest='experiment_id',required=True)
        s.add_argument('--analysis',required=True);s.add_argument('--pvt',required=True)
        s.add_argument('--cl',type=float,help='Load capacitance in farads')
        s.add_argument('--seed',type=int)
    sub.add_parser('submit').add_argument('--rationale',required=True)
    return p


def request_from(args,workspace):
    if args.request:
        if args.command:raise ValueError('--request cannot be combined with a command')
        request=json.loads(args.request.read_text())
    else:
        request={'action':args.command or 'status'}
        for key in ('experiment_id','analysis','pvt','cl','seed','rationale'):
            value=getattr(args,key,None)
            if value is not None:request[key]=value
    if not isinstance(request,dict):raise ValueError('Request must be a JSON object')
    if request.get('action') not in ('help','status','validate','estimate','measure','submit'):
        raise ValueError('Unknown participant action')
    if request['action'] in ('validate','measure','submit'):
        task=workspace/'task.json'
        if task.exists() and json.loads(task.read_text()).get('design_format')=='netlist':
            request['design']={'netlist':(workspace/'dut.spice').read_bytes().decode('utf-8')}
        else:request['design']=json.loads((workspace/'design.json').read_text())
    return request


def exchange(request,address):
    with socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX,socket.SOCK_STREAM) as sock:
        sock.connect(str(address))
        sock.sendall((json.dumps(request,allow_nan=False)+'\n').encode())
        with sock.makefile('r') as stream:
            reply=json.loads(stream.readline())
    if not isinstance(reply,dict):raise ValueError('Broker reply must be a JSON object')
    return reply


def main(argv=None,workspace=Path('/workspace'),address=Path('/run/atb/broker.sock')):
    args=parser().parse_args(argv)
    try:reply=exchange(request_from(args,Path(workspace)),address)
    except (OSError,ValueError,UnicodeError) as exc:
        # Do not include request contents, circuit bytes or provider credentials.
        reply={'ok':False,'error':type(exc).__name__,'reason':'Cannot read the request/design or exchange a valid broker reply.'}
    print(json.dumps(reply,ensure_ascii=False,indent=2,allow_nan=False))
    return 0 if reply.get('ok') is True else 1


if __name__=='__main__':sys.exit(main())

MODEL

The first nominal run regulated accurately and stayed far below the overhead limit, but the 30 pF compensation caused strong ringing. Removing it improved PSRR and reduced output noise, though transients still settle too slowly. I’m increasing the amplifier’s available current and speeding the pass gate’s pull-up to improve slew and damping while keeping the light-load budget in view.

MODEL

The gate driver stage appears to be the source of much of the ringing and noise. I’m trying a single-stage error amplifier that drives the pass gate directly, with a mirrored sink sized to handle gate pull-up current. That removes an internal high-gain stage and its extra pole.

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS reference current and differential pair
RBIAS PB VSS 50k
XPBIAS PB PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPTAIL CS PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Feedback divider targets VOUT=2*VREF
RFTOP VOUT FB 100k
RFBOT FB VSS 100k
* P-channel input pair; N-channel mirror produces an increasing output
* command when VOUT is below target.
XPMREF N1 VREF CS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=40 l=2
XPMFB N2 FB CS VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=40 l=2
XNMREF N1 N1 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=2
XNMFDB N2 N1 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=20 l=2
* NMOS driver sinks the pass gate; a PMOS current source restores it off.
XDRV PGATE N2 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=1
XPGUP PGATE PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=2 m=2
C2 N2 VSS 10p
* High-side pass device
XPASS VOUT PGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=16
.ends DUT

MODEL

Larger PMOS input devices reduced noise but damaged 1 MHz PSRR through supply coupling. I’m switching to an NMOS input pair referenced to ground, retaining the PMOS pass device and current source gate pull-up. This should isolate the sensing stage from VIN; I’ll check whether the 0.6 V common-mode leaves enough margin in the slow corner.

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF

XPGUP PGATE PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=2 m=2
* NMOS tail current reference and sink
RBIASN VIN NB 100k
XBIASN NB NB VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XTAIL NT NB VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Feedback divider targets VOUT = 2*VREF
RFTOP VOUT FB 100k
RFBOT FB VSS 100k
* Ground-referenced NMOS differential pair with PMOS mirror load
XNMREF D1 VREF NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XNMFDB D2 FB NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XPMREF D1 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPMOUT D2 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Error stage pulls the pass gate down; current source restores it high.
XDRV PGATE D2 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=1
XPASS VOUT PGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=16
.ends DUT
EOF"

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS gate pull-up reference and current source
RBIASP PB VSS 50k
XPBIAS PB PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPGUP PGATE PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
* NMOS tail current reference and sink
RBIASN VIN NB 25k
XBIASN NB NB VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XTAIL NT NB VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Feedback divider targets VOUT = 2*VREF
RFTOP VOUT FB 100k
RFBOT FB VSS 100k
CFF VOUT FB 100p
* Ground-referenced NMOS differential pair with PMOS mirror load
XNMREF D1 VREF NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XNMFDB D2 FB NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XPMREF D1 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=4
XPMOUT D2 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=4
* Error stage pulls the pass gate down; current source restores it high.
XDRV PGATE D2 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=1
XPASS VOUT PGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=16
.ends DUT

MODEL

The NMOS input architecture is now close on noise and accurate regulation, but the line step still causes too much overshoot. I’m adding a small VIN-to-pass-gate feed-forward capacitor so the PMOS gate follows supply edges before the feedback loop reacts, while retaining the output-to-feedback capacitor that reduced noise.

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS gate pull-up reference and current source
RBIASP PB VSS 50k
XPBIAS PB PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPGUP PGATE PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
* NMOS tail current reference and sink
RBIASN VIN NB 25k
XBIASN NB NB VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XTAIL NT NB VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Feedback divider targets VOUT = 2*VREF
RFTOP VOUT FB 100k
RFBOT FB VSS 100k
CFF VOUT FB 10p
CVINFB VIN FB 10p
* Ground-referenced NMOS differential pair with PMOS mirror load
XNMREF D1 VREF NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XNMFDB D2 FB NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XPMREF D1 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPMOUT D2 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Error stage pulls the pass gate down; current source restores it high.
XDRV PGATE D2 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=1
XPASS VOUT PGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=16
.ends DUT

.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF
* PMOS gate pull-up reference and current source
RBIASP PB VSS 50k
XPBIAS PB PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPGUP PGATE PB VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Reference-driven NMOS tail current sink
XTAIL NT VREF VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=4 m=10
* Feedback divider targets VOUT = 2*VREF
RFTOP VOUT FB 100k
RFBOT FB VSS 100k
CFF VOUT FB 10p
* Ground-referenced NMOS differential pair with PMOS mirror load
XNMREF D1 VREF NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XNMFDB D2 FB NT VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=2
XPMREF D1 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
XPMOUT D2 D1 VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=50 l=2
* Error stage pulls the pass gate down; current source restores it high.
XDRV PGATE D2 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w=100 l=1
XPASS VOUT PGATE VIN VIN sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w=100 l=0.5 m=16
.ends DUT

The 0.6 V reference can bias the NMOS tail directly with zero reference current, giving much more light-load overhead margin. Nominal output noise is now below 30 µV RMS, and 1 MHz PSRR passes. The remaining misses are line transient amplitude, 1 kHz PSRR, and recovery time; I’m testing gate-drive strength before freezing the design.

# Shared client

Write request.json and call `atb-client --request request.json`.
Commands: `atb-client help`, `atb-client status`, `atb-client validate`,
`atb-client estimate --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client measure --id m001 --analysis nominal --pvt N`,
`atb-client submit --rationale "Design rationale"`.
Use `--cl` in farads and optional `--seed` only when the task supports it.
The client reads dut.spice once for validate/measure/submit and sends its exact UTF-8 contents.
Measure requires experiment_id, analysis and pvt; cl is optional. Use help for analyses and native case costs.
Use a new experiment_id when changing a circuit or measurement request. Completed identical requests reuse their saved result.
Submit requires rationale. Successful submission freezes that circuit for every independent condition and closes exploration.

## Public measurement options

| Analysis | PVT | Load (F) | Cases | Included native measurements |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| nominal | N, SLC, SLH, SHC, SHH, FLC, FLH, FHC, FHH | 1e-07 | 11 | dc_low, dc_mid, dc_high, light_heavy, mid_heavy, burst, psrr_low, psrr_high, noise_low, noise_high, line |

One native case is one simulator process. Bundled internal analyses are retained in evidence.
`estimate` returns the exact case plan without launching a solver. Independent evaluation conditions are not available to participants.
# LDO-QUIET-SKY130 measurement contract

Numerical stimuli and limits come from spec.json. Connect the same submitted
DUT to VIN, VOUT, VSS and ideal noiseless VREF. The load is a prescribed ideal
finite-slew current sink; the external capacitor is ideal and bench supplied.
No startup, protection, bandgap, yield or layout checks are implied.

## DC and load changes

Run DC at all three loads and light/heavy, middle/heavy and burst profiles.
Meter all DUT terminals. Input/reference currents enter DUT; output/ground
currents leave. Verify KCL within 1 nA. Overhead is
max(Iin-Iout,0)+max(Iref,0), including feedback and bias consumption.
Compare voltage against the fixed 1.2 V target, never the waveform tail.
Both isolated edge directions and the final falling burst edge have recovery
windows. Recovery is the final interpolated entry into the absolute required
band that remains there until the window ends. Retain overshoot, droop, initial
hold error, profile points and all signed currents.

Maximum sample gap is 1e-08 s. Every required window must be fully
covered with finite increasing data. Unsettled complete data retains null
recovery and an observation lower bound; it is MISS when that bound exceeds the
limit. Missing/truncated/invalid data is measurement failure. Unexecuted cases
are incomplete, never PASS. Inclusive limits are compared without rounding.

## Supply measurements

Line stimulus starts at minimum VIN, rises to maximum, and returns to minimum,
at the group's highest load, process, temperature and capacitance. The starting
VIN label does not add a different line trajectory. PSRR saves native VIN/VOUT
phasors at 1 kHz and 1 MHz and reports 20 log10(abs(VIN/VOUT)). Check the native
regulated OP; zero/nonfinite transfers cannot produce infinite rejection.

PSRR, bidirectional line excursion/recovery and output noise are scored in every
public and independent group. Each nominal group contains 11 native processes:
three DC, three load profiles, two PSRR, two noise and one line profile.
There are 198 public plus 33 independent cases, with no duplicate nominal
characterization stage. Standalone noise_low/noise_high/line/PSRR cost one each.
Line uses the tighter line excursion limit; its initial and recovery bands are
the fixed DC/recovery bands. Repeated endpoint trajectories across starting-VIN
labels are repetitions, not extra coverage.

Output noise integrates native output voltage ASD squared from 10 Hz to 100 kHz
at 50 points/decade. Use a linear-frequency trapezoidal PSD integral and then its
square root. VREF and load are ideal noiseless sources. Keep the spectrum in
V/sqrt(Hz), integrated output in V RMS, and a valid regulated OP. Negative ASD,
missing band endpoints, sparse/nonfinite data and nonregulating OP cannot pass.

## Numerical precision

Independent evaluation uses the captured standard grid for every required case.
Numerical precision comparisons use a separately authorized developer allocation.
A standard-grid PASS is not a per-submission convergence proof.
# LDO-QUIET-SKY130

Design a continuous-time analog LDO meeting spec.json across conditions.json and the specified load range.
Create dut.spice with `.subckt DUT VIN VOUT VSS VREF` and `.ends DUT`.
Choose connectivity, bias, compensation and dimensions yourself. No starting circuit is supplied.
Use only the declared MOS family and positive R/C in devices.md. Read measurement.md.
You have 90 minutes of cumulative model-call time with no native-case limit. Use the client to measure and submit your fixed circuit before the deadline.
No Web search. Use only the provided task information and your own knowledge.
Measurements consume cases even when simulation fails. Submit through the client with a rationale, then end your session.

## Time accounting

The budget counts model calls, including provider queuing and transport. ngspice, Python, filesystem tools and their waits do not consume this budget. Model calls overlapping local tools still count. An already admitted measurement may finish after model-budget exhaustion; new design tools close. Use client status for the latest collected model-time reading.

MODEL

The slow line recovery appears tied to the pass-gate pull-up: the present PMOS current source does not track VIN, so a rising supply feeds through the pass device before the loop corrects it. I’m trying a VIN-to-gate resistor pull-up, which should make the pass device turn down sooner during a line rise and reduce bias current.

Lengthening the NMOS input pair and its gate driver raised nominal 1 kHz PSRR above 41 dB and kept output noise and overhead within spec. The line recovery metric is actually measuring the output’s error while VIN stays at its high level; the remaining excess is about 2.6 mV. I’m combining that higher-gain amplifier with VIN tracking at the pass gate, then I’ll recheck the full nominal bundle.

MODEL

The best response shape so far is with the stronger 12 kΩ pull-up, but reducing tail multiplicity to save current also worsened the line waveform. I’m holding the same tail W/L ratio at a longer channel length to retain current capability with less tail current, then centering the small remaining VIN error by shifting the feedback ratio slightly below 2:1.

The VOUT-to-gate path cut overhead to about 77 µA and preserved load recovery. Increasing the input pair length to 5 µm brought both 1 kHz PSRR readings above 40 dB, but pushed the high-line peak just outside the recovery band. import json, subprocess, pathlib
for pvt in ['SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']:
  for cl in [1e-7,1e-6]:
    exp=f'trial61_{pvt.lower()}_cl{int(cl*1e9)}n'
    req={'action':'measure','experiment_id':exp,'analysis':'nominal','pvt':pvt,'cl':cl}
    pathlib.Path('REQUEST.json').write_text(json.dumps(req))
    p=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],text=True,capture_output=True)
    try: r=json.loads(p.stdout)
    except Exception:
      print(exp,'CLIENT_ERROR',p.returncode,p.stderr[:300],flush=True);continue
    pathlib.Path(exp+'.json').write_text(json.dumps(r,indent=2))
    misses=[x for x in r.get('summary',{}).get('spec_table',[]) if x.get('verdict')"'!='"'PASS']
    budget=r.get('budget',{}).get('remaining_seconds')
    print(exp,'ok',r.get('ok'),'cases',r.get('cases_reserved'),'misses',len(misses),'remaining_s',round(budget,1) if budget is not None else None,flush=True)
    for x in misses[:10]:
      print(' ',x.get('case_id'),x.get('metric'),x.get('measured'),x.get('limit'),x.get('verdict'),flush=True)
PY"
MODEL

The nominal N result passes, but the first slow low-supply corners show lower 1 kHz PSRR and higher light-load overhead; 100 nF also misses 1 MHz PSRR and line recovery at the cold corner. The 1 µF runs are cleaner so far. I’m finishing the corner sweep to see whether these misses are localized before revising the design.

The full public sweep is complete. Several low-supply slow/fast corners still miss light-load overhead and 1 kHz PSRR; some also miss line recovery. The 8 kΩ VOUT feedback candidate passes all nominal N cases, while every 1 µF case except the slow-high-cold 1 kHz point passed. I’m trying a small source resistor at the NMOS tail to reduce tail-current spread over process and temperature, then I’ll remeasure the worst corners.

MODEL

The 11 kΩ/fast-driver revision reduces low-supply light-load overhead, but corner PSRR remains the main gap. A 1 kΩ tail source resistor reduced nominal overhead on the previous topology; I’m combining it with the faster driver and longer mirror to see whether the high-speed path preserves recovery while tail current varies less across corners.

Adding the tail resistor and tuning the feedback ratio produced a nominal pass again. Candidate 76 also clears line recovery at the high-line edge, with light-load overhead near 72.5 µA and 1 kHz PSRR above 41 dB. I’m running the public corners on this version now; if the low-supply PSRR spread still remains, I’ll freeze the best measured result before the budget closes.

for pvt in ['SLC','SLH','SHC','SHH','FLC','FLH','FHC','FHH']:

    p=subprocess.run(['atb-client','--request','REQUEST.json'],text=True,capture_output=True)
